## Phase 4 Context

### Milestone Scope Context

Gathered: 2026-06-03
Calibration: builder

## Scope Boundary

**Board Refinements** — a set of post-ship tweaks and fixes to the Project Board
("Planner") shipped in the previous milestone. Four user-requested changes:
1. Archive a card without typing the project name (drop the type-to-confirm gate).
2. Add a new board column/stage: "Stopped".
3. Fix: any user with access to a card can download any file on it (not only files they uploaded).
4. Auto-scroll the board horizontally while dragging a card near the edge.

## Decomposition Decisions

### Phase Count & Grouping
Three phases. The two board-UI changes (Stopped column #2 + horizontal drag
auto-scroll #4) are grouped into Phase 1 because they share the same surface —
the Kanban board's stage list and drag context (`Board.tsx`, `KanbanColumn`,
stage types, and the backend stage enum/validation) — so doing them together
avoids file conflicts and lets them share one QA/UAT pass. The archive change (#1)
and the file-download fix (#3) are independent concerns touching disjoint files
(ArchiveCardDialog/admin-archive route vs. the file-download route/service), so
each is its own phase for clean, independent verification.

### Phase Ordering
1. **Stopped column + drag auto-scroll** — largest (spans frontend stage model +
   backend stage enum); do the structural board change first.
2. **Archive without typed confirmation** — small, self-contained frontend+backend.
3. **File download permission fix** — small backend access-control fix.
No hard dependencies between phases; ordered by size/risk (biggest first).

### Scope Coverage
**Covers:** the four changes above. **Excludes:** the carried follow-ups from the
prior milestone (schedule→board live-refresh on assignment create; SQLite
single-writer concurrency) — not requested in this batch. The empty-projectName
archive edge case is naturally resolved by Phase 2.

## Requirement Mapping

| Phase | Change(s) | Area |
|-------|-----------|------|
| 1 — Stopped Column & Drag Auto-Scroll | #2 Stopped column, #4 horizontal drag auto-scroll | Board stages, drag-and-drop UX |
| 2 — Archive Without Typed Confirmation | #1 archive without project name | Board archive UX, access control |
| 3 — File Download Permission Fix | #3 download any card file | Board files, access control |

## Key Decisions

- **Archive keeps a lightweight confirm.** Archive permanently deletes files, so
  Phase 2 drops only the typed-name gate, not the confirmation step itself
  (Archive/Cancel remains). To be confirmed in discussion.
- **"Stopped" is a manual stage.** Auto-move must not override a card the user
  manually placed in "Stopped". Exact column position in the stage order to be
  confirmed in discussion.
- **NON-NEGOTIABLE schedule isolation** continues for all board work: no writes
  to Assignment/TeamMember/Absence/Holiday (carried from the Project Board milestone).

## Deferred Ideas

- Schedule→board live-refresh when an assignment is created (carried follow-up).
- SQLite single-writer concurrency hardening at the product level (carried follow-up).


### Goal
On the board (Kanban) cards, replace the textual pentester name(s) line with small circular profile-picture avatars — one per pentester — reusing the same avatar logic the schedule already uses (the `avatarUrl` at `/uploads/avatars/<userId>` with an initials fallback when no picture). Project Name and Client Name lines stay as text; only the pentester line becomes avatars.

### Research Findings
---
phase: "04"
title: "Board Card Pentester Avatars"
type: research
confidence: high
date: 2026-06-03
---

## Findings

### 1. Schedule avatar rendering — the reuse target

**File:** `frontend/src/features/schedule/components/ScheduleGrid.tsx`, lines 851–858

The schedule's row header renders each team member's avatar inline inside `renderTable()`:

```tsx
// ScheduleGrid.tsx lines 851–858
{member.user?.avatarUrl ? (
  <img src={member.user.avatarUrl} alt="" className="w-9 h-9 rounded-full shrink-0 object-cover" />
) : (
  <div className="w-9 h-9 rounded-full shrink-0 bg-slate-300 dark:bg-slate-600 flex items-center justify-center text-sm font-semibold text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-300">
    {(member.displayName || member.user?.displayName || member.user?.username || '?').charAt(0).toUpperCase()}
  </div>
)}
```

This is NOT using the shadcn `Avatar`/`AvatarImage`/`AvatarFallback` primitives — it is a hand-rolled inline pattern: a plain `<img>` for the image branch and a `<div>` for the initials-fallback branch. The pattern is fully self-contained and portable.

**Avatar source:** `member.user?.avatarUrl` — a URL string stored directly on the `User` record, populated by `POST /api/profile/avatar`. The upload stores the file to `uploads/avatars/<userId>.<ext>` on disk and writes `/uploads/avatars/<userId>.<ext>?t=<timestamp>` into `User.avatarUrl` (`profile.ts` lines 136–138). The `uploads` directory is served statically at `/uploads` (excluding `/uploads/board` which is 403'd) — so `avatarUrl` is a simple relative path and `<img src={avatarUrl}>` works directly from the browser.

**Initials fallback:** single initial from `displayName` (override display name on the `TeamMember`) or `user.displayName` or `user.username`, uppercased. The `?` sentinel covers `TeamMember` backlog placeholders (no linked user, no displayName).

**Sizing classes used in the schedule:** `w-9 h-9` (36 × 36 px). For the board card a smaller size is appropriate — `w-6 h-6` or `w-7 h-7` would match the card's compact layout.

**shadcn Avatar primitives** (`components/ui/avatar.tsx`) also exist in the project and expose `Avatar` (root, `size="sm"` = 24 px / `size="default"` = 32 px / `size="lg"` = 40 px), `AvatarImage`, `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarGroup` (stacked row with `ring-2` separation), and `AvatarGroupCount` (overflow badge). These primitives are Radix-based and Tailwind-styled. The board card could either use these primitives (cleaner, consistent with the design system) or copy the hand-rolled inline pattern from the schedule. Using the shadcn primitives is recommended — see Recommendations.

**Multiple avatars (AvatarGroup):** The shadcn `AvatarGroup` component (`avatar.tsx` lines 71–82) renders `*[data-slot=avatar]` children with `flex -space-x-2 *[data-slot=avatar]:ring-2` — i.e. a horizontally-overlapping stack with `ring-background` gaps. The schedule grid does NOT currently use `AvatarGroup`; it shows exactly one avatar per row (one team member per row). The board card, however, must handle multiple pentesters — the `AvatarGroup` primitive is the correct pick here.

---

### 2. Board card current pentester rendering

**File:** `frontend/src/features/board/components/KanbanCard.tsx`, lines 98–113

```tsx
{/* Row 2: client + pentester list (Phase 24-R03) */}
{(card.project.client?.name || card.assignments.length > 0) && (
  <div className="text-xs text-muted-foreground space-y-0.5">
    {card.project.client?.name && <p>{card.project.client.name}</p>}
    {card.assignments.length > 0 && (
      <p className="line-clamp-1">
        {Array.from(
          new Set(
            card.assignments
              .map((a) => a.teamMember?.displayName ?? a.teamMember?.user?.displayName ?? a.teamMember?.user?.username ?? a.teamMemberId)
              .filter(Boolean),
          ),
        ).join(', ')}
      </p>
    )}
  </div>
)}
```

The pentester row (lines 103–112) maps `card.assignments` → display name (with fallback chain) → deduplicates with `Set` → joins as comma-separated text in a `<p>` with `line-clamp-1`. The `<p>` element and its text must be replaced with the avatar group.

**Data shape available per assignment** (`frontend/src/features/board/types.ts`, lines 43–53):

```ts
export interface BoardCardAssignment {
  assignmentId: string
  teamMemberId: string
  weekStart: string
  side: 'primary' | 'secondary'
  teamMember: {
    userId: string | null
    displayName: string | null
    user: { displayName: string | null; username: string } | null
  } | null
}
```

The `teamMember` object currently exposes: `userId`, `displayName` (on the `TeamMember` row itself), and `user.displayName` / `user.username`. There is **no `avatarUrl` field** anywhere in `BoardCardAssignment.teamMember.user` — this is the data gap.

**memo comparator** (`KanbanCard.tsx` lines 133–141): the existing comparator already re-renders when `card.assignments.length` changes. A new `avatarUrl` field in assignments would require adding an avatar-equality check here (or using a simple deep-equal of `card.assignments`).

---

### 3. Data gap analysis

**VERDICT: DATA GAP — a backend payload change IS required.**

The current `ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT` constant in `boardService.ts` (lines 79–85) is:

```ts
const ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT = {
  select: {
    userId: true,
    displayName: true,
    user: { select: { displayName: true, username: true } },
  },
} as const;
```

It does NOT select `user.avatarUrl`. This constant is used by both `listCards` (line 103–104 and 106–107) and `getCard` (lines 143–144 and 146–147).

The schedule's `scheduleService.listTeamMembers()` DOES select `avatarUrl`:

```ts
// scheduleService.ts lines 12–14
user: {
  select: { username: true, displayName: true, avatarUrl: true },
},
```

So the avatar URL is already in the database and is already served to the schedule view — it is simply not fetched by the board service.

**What to add — minimal backend change:**

1. In `backend/src/services/boardService.ts`, update `ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT` to add `avatarUrl: true` into the `user` sub-select:

```ts
// BEFORE (lines 79–85)
const ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT = {
  select: {
    userId: true,
    displayName: true,
    user: { select: { displayName: true, username: true } },
  },
} as const;

// AFTER
const ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT = {
  select: {
    userId: true,
    displayName: true,
    user: { select: { displayName: true, username: true, avatarUrl: true } },
  },
} as const;
```

This is a read-only `select` expansion on an existing `include`. It touches no write path. The `shapeAssignmentForCard` function (lines 44–77) passes `teamMember: a.teamMember` through as-is, so the extra field propagates automatically without touching `shapeAssignmentForCard`.

2. In `frontend/src/features/board/types.ts`, update `BoardCardAssignment.teamMember.user` to include the new field:

```ts
// BEFORE (lines 48–52)
teamMember: {
  userId: string | null
  displayName: string | null
  user: { displayName: string | null; username: string } | null
} | null

// AFTER
teamMember: {
  userId: string | null
  displayName: string | null
  user: { displayName: string | null; username: string; avatarUrl: string | null } | null
} | null
```

**Schedule-isolation invariant check:** The `boardService.ts` file contains no explicit "NON-NEGOTIABLE" schedule-isolation guard on the `listCards` / `getCard` read path (those guards live on write paths in `assignmentService.ts`). The proposed change is a pure `select` addition on the existing `include: { teamMember: ... }` that already traverses `Assignment → TeamMember → User`. It does NOT write any schedule table, does not add joins across isolation boundaries, and cannot cause cascade mutations. The `scheduleIsolation.phase24` test (`boardService.ts` does not write `TeamMember` / `Absence` / `Holiday`) remains valid. No isolation risk.

---

### 4. Profile picture storage and serving

**Prisma model** (`schema.prisma` line 30): `User.avatarUrl String?` — a nullable string. Stores a relative URL path.

**Upload flow** (`routes/profile.ts` lines 12–140): Files are uploaded to `uploads/avatars/<userId>.<ext>` on disk. The stored URL is `/uploads/avatars/<userId>.<ext>?t=<timestamp>` (with a cache-busting query param).

**Static serving** (`index.ts` line 118): `app.use('/uploads', express.static(...))` serves the whole `uploads/` tree publicly — avatars are NOT gated by auth (unlike board files). So `avatarUrl` can be used directly as an `<img src>` in the browser.

**Backlog placeholders:** `TeamMember.userId` is nullable (schema line 170). A backlog member has no linked `User`, so `teamMember.user` is `null` and `avatarUrl` is unavailable — these must fall back to initials. The initials fallback uses `teamMember.displayName` (which backlog members always have, e.g. "Futuro 1").

**Do team members have profile pictures in practice?** The feature exists and is used (the schedule renders `member.user?.avatarUrl` already), but not all users will have uploaded one — `avatarUrl` is frequently `null`. The board must match the schedule's behavior: show the picture if present, show a single initial if not.

---

### 5. Multiple pentesters per card

A card can have multiple `BoardCardAssignment` entries — both `primaryAssignments` and `splitAssignments` are included. A card with a split assignment (two projects sharing one week) may yield one entry from `primaryAssignments` and one from `splitAssignments` for different `teamMemberId`s. Beyond that, multiple pentesters can each have separate assignments in different weeks that all link to the same project.

The current code deduplicates by display name; the avatar approach should deduplicate by `teamMemberId` to avoid showing the same person twice.

**Stacked overlapping row:** the shadcn `AvatarGroup` (`avatar.tsx` lines 71–82) is the right primitive. It uses `flex -space-x-2` (2 px negative space between circles) with a `ring-2 ring-background` separator on each avatar. With `size="sm"` (24 × 24 px), 3–4 avatars fit cleanly in the card's compact layout. If there are more than a practical cap (e.g. > 3 or > 4), `AvatarGroupCount` can show "+N" overflow.

The schedule grid does NOT have a multi-avatar group on the card (it's one avatar per row). The `AvatarGroup` stacking behaviour is novel to this phase but the component is already in the repo.

---

### 6. Tests and frontend conventions

**Existing KanbanCard tests:** There is currently only ONE frontend test file in `frontend/src`: `features/adapter/components/__tests__/MappingOverlayCard.test.tsx`. No `KanbanCard.test.tsx` or `KanbanCard.spec.tsx` exists in `frontend/src`. The phase-01 board work that added `KanbanCard` did not create a co-located unit test file for it.

**Backend board tests:**
- `backend/src/services/__tests__/boardAutoMove.stopped.test.ts` — integration test for `autoMoveCards()`
- `backend/src/routes/__tests__/boardAdminArchive.test.ts` — route integration
- `backend/src/routes/__tests__/boardFiles.test.ts` — file upload/download
- `backend/src/services/__tests__/scheduleIsolation.phase24.test.ts` — isolation regression

**Test runner:** Vitest (`vitest.config.ts` in both `backend/` and `frontend/`). Frontend: `jsdom` environment, `globals: true`, `setupFiles: ['./src/test-setup.ts']`, includes `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`.

**What a new KanbanCard test should assert:**
- Given a card with 2 distinct pentesters (each with `teamMember.user.avatarUrl` set), the rendered output contains 2 avatar images (or AvatarFallback initials when `avatarUrl` is null), NOT a text string of names.
- Given a card with 0 pentesters, no avatar group is rendered.
- Given pentesters where all `avatarUrl` are null, initials-fallback elements render (one per unique `teamMemberId`).
- The old text-join (`join(', ')`) no longer appears in the output.
- The memo comparator re-renders when an assignment's `avatarUrl` changes (regression guard).

**Existing adapter test pattern** (`MappingOverlayCard.test.tsx`) uses `@testing-library/react` + `render`/`screen` queries — follow that convention.

---

## Relevant Patterns

- **Schedule avatar inline pattern** (ScheduleGrid lines 851–858): conditional `<img src={avatarUrl}>` / `<div>` initials — the proven reuse target. Hand-rolled, not using shadcn primitives. Sizing: `w-9 h-9`.
- **shadcn Avatar primitives** (`components/ui/avatar.tsx`): `Avatar` (sizes `sm`=24px, `default`=32px, `lg`=40px), `AvatarImage`, `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarGroup` (overlapping flex stack), `AvatarGroupCount` (overflow "+N"). These exist and are unused by the schedule — the board is the natural first consumer of `AvatarGroup`.
- **ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT** in `boardService.ts` (line 79): a named constant shared by `listCards` and `getCard` — updating it once in one place propagates to both endpoints, which is the minimal correct approach.
- **boardService schedule-isolation:** write paths (upsert, update) in `assignmentService.ts` carry the isolation invariant, not the read paths in `boardService.ts`. Read-only `select` expansion is safe.
- **KanbanCard memo comparator** (lines 133–141): checks `card.assignments.length` but not the content of each assignment. After adding `avatarUrl`, the comparator either needs to check equality of avatar fields or a shallow per-assignment comparison should be added to prevent stale avatars after an upload.

---

## Risks

1. **Memo comparator staleness.** The `KanbanCard` custom `areEqual` comparator (lines 133–141) only compares `card.assignments.length`. If a pentester uploads a new avatar after the card is mounted, the component will not re-render because the new `avatarUrl` is not compared. Mitigation: add `prev.card.assignments === next.card.assignments` (reference equality via React Query's normalized cache) or serialize assignment identities. The safest approach is to compare a small, stable fingerprint (e.g. join of `teamMemberId + (avatarUrl ?? '')`).

2. **AvatarGroup overflow.** A project with many pentesters (5+) would overflow the card width with the `AvatarGroup` approach. A cap of 3 visible + overflow count is advisable for a compact card layout, using `AvatarGroupCount`.

3. **Backlog members / null user.** When `teamMember.user` is `null` (backlog placeholder), `avatarUrl` is unavailable. The initials fallback must use `teamMember.displayName`, which is always set for backlog rows. Do not fall back to `teamMemberId` (an opaque cuid) as the schedule code currently does via `a.teamMemberId` in the `??` chain.

4. **Deduplication logic change.** The current code deduplicates by display name (using a `Set` of strings). With avatars, deduplication must switch to `teamMemberId` to avoid showing the same person twice when they have both a primary and split assignment on the same card.

5. **No existing KanbanCard frontend test.** There is no `KanbanCard.test.tsx` to extend or use as a reference. Phase 4 must create one from scratch, following the `MappingOverlayCard.test.tsx` pattern.

6. **Cache-busting on avatarUrl.** The stored `avatarUrl` contains a `?t=<timestamp>` query string (set at upload time, not at request time). After a user re-uploads their avatar, existing board cards in React Query's cache will still show the old URL until the cache is invalidated. This is the same behavior the schedule has today — no special action needed for Phase 4, but note it for future UX improvement.

---

## Recommendations

### Backend change (required)

**File:** `backend/src/services/boardService.ts`, lines 79–85.

Add `avatarUrl: true` to the `user` sub-select in `ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT`:

```ts
const ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT = {
  select: {
    userId: true,
    displayName: true,
    user: { select: { displayName: true, username: true, avatarUrl: true } },
  },
} as const;
```

This single-line change propagates to `listCards` and `getCard` automatically. No other backend change needed. Schedule isolation is unaffected.

### Frontend type change (required)

**File:** `frontend/src/features/board/types.ts`, line 51.

Add `avatarUrl: string | null` to `BoardCardAssignment.teamMember.user`.

### Frontend component change (required)

**File:** `frontend/src/features/board/components/KanbanCard.tsx`, lines 103–112.

Replace the text-join `<p>` with an `AvatarGroup` rendered from a deduplicated-by-`teamMemberId` list. Use the shadcn `Avatar` + `AvatarImage` + `AvatarFallback` + `AvatarGroup` primitives (already in the repo) rather than the hand-rolled `<img>`/`<div>` inline style from the schedule. Import from `@/components/ui/avatar`.

**Recommended size:** `size="sm"` (24 × 24 px) — fits compactly in the card's content row.

**Recommended cap:** render up to 3 avatars, then an `AvatarGroupCount` showing "+N" for the remainder.

**Initials fallback:** `(teamMember.displayName || teamMember.user?.displayName || teamMember.user?.username || '?').charAt(0).toUpperCase()` — same logic the schedule uses.

**Memo comparator update:** Update the `areEqual` comparator to also compare a stable avatar identity fingerprint, e.g.:

```ts
prev.card.assignments.map(a => a.teamMemberId + (a.teamMember?.user?.avatarUrl ?? '')).join() ===
next.card.assignments.map(a => a.teamMemberId + (a.teamMember?.user?.avatarUrl ?? '')).join()
```

### Frontend test (required)

Create `frontend/src/features/board/components/__tests__/KanbanCard.test.tsx` (new file, co-located in a `__tests__/` subdir following the adapter pattern). Assert: avatar images/initials render instead of text; deduplication by `teamMemberId` works; null `avatarUrl` shows initials; 0 assignments shows nothing.

## Data Gap

**VERDICT: NO** — the board card payload does NOT currently carry avatar data.

The `ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT` constant in `boardService.ts` selects `user.displayName` and `user.username` but omits `user.avatarUrl`. The `BoardCardAssignment.teamMember.user` type in `board/types.ts` has no `avatarUrl` field.

**Exact fix:** add `avatarUrl: true` to the `user` sub-select in `ASSIGNMENT_TEAM_MEMBER_SELECT` (boardService.ts line 83) and add `avatarUrl: string | null` to the TypeScript type (board/types.ts line 51). The underlying data is already in the `User` table and is already served to the schedule — this is a query narrowing omission, not a schema or migration gap.
